`AGENTS.md`:

```md
# rea-games: notes for coding agents

Read `skills/rea-games/SKILL.md` first; it is the workflow. Short version of the rules:

- Run `node bin/rea-games.mjs verify all` before saying anything works. Quote its summary line, not a paraphrase.
- Traces in `games/*/cases/` are recordings of the original. Never edit one by hand; run `rea-games record <game>`.
- A port is "verified" only when `verify` runs it through its runner and every case is identical.
- No game art, audio, names or code from an original goes into a port unless the original's licence allows it (see `NOTICE`).
- Keep `NOTICE`, `docs/STATUS.md` and the README numbers in step with what `verify` prints.
- Mistakes worth not repeating go in `docs/pitfalls.md` in the same change.

```

`CONTRIBUTING.md`:

```md
# Contributing to rea-games

The most useful contribution is **a new game that passes its own recording**, or **a new engine port of an existing one**.

## Add a game

1. Pick a game whose source you may run and redistribute (MIT, BSD, Apache, public domain). Say which licence in the issue first. No commercial games, no trademarked names, no art or sound from the original.
2. `node bin/rea-games.mjs new <game>` and read `skills/rea-games/SKILL.md`: it is the whole workflow.
3. Vendor the original unmodified under `originals/<game>` with its licence, and add a line to `NOTICE`.
4. Record it (`record.mjs`), write `GAME.md`, write the port, and make `node bin/rea-games.mjs verify <game>` print every case identical.
5. Break the port on purpose in at least three ways and show `verify` fails each time (put the numbers in the PR).
6. `node bin/rea-games.mjs pack <game>` before committing; cases are stored gzipped.

## Add an engine port

A port is any program that reads a case on stdin and prints `{trace, tapeUsed}` (see `games/2048/ports/godot/runner.gd` and `games/2048/ports/rust/src/main.rs`). Add it to the game's `game.json`. It counts as verified only when `verify` passes it.

## Rules

- Never edit a recording by hand, and never loosen a comparison to get green.
- Report numbers as `verify` printed them, including what is not covered.
- Add a mistake worth not repeating to `docs/pitfalls.md` in the same change.

```

`DECISIONS.md`:

```md
# Decisions

Choices and the reason for each. Change one only with a reason of the same weight.

**The proof is a recording, not a code comparison.** The same idea as rust-anything: run the original, save what it does,
and check every rebuild against the saved behavior. A rebuild passes only when every recorded state is identical.

**Random numbers are recorded, not seeded.** A port cannot reproduce a different language's generator, so the case
holds the numbers the original drew (the `tape`) and the port reads them back in order. A port that asks for more or
fewer numbers than the original used fails.

**The original is never edited.** It runs as downloaded; only its clock, its random numbers and its browser surface are
replaced from outside. A recording of a patched game proves nothing about the real one.

**Random numbers that cannot change play get their own stream.** Clouds and stars in Dino draw from `Math.random` too.
The recorder tells the callers apart (by stack) and gives the cosmetic ones a separate generator, so the port does not
have to copy drawing code to stay in step. Each game's `GAME.md` says what was split and shows the trace does not change
when the cosmetic stream does.

**Runner protocol: JSON in, JSON out.** A port is any program that reads a case on stdin and prints `{trace, tapeUsed}`.
That makes Rust, GDScript run headless, C# and a browser port all checkable by the same code.

**Node for the tool, no dependencies.** The CLI and recorders are plain Node 22 with no npm packages (Playwright is used
for the browser games and is already on most machines that develop for the web). Contributors who build engine ports do
not need a Rust or Node expertise to run `verify`.

**Web first, then engines.** A browser port is playable from a link, which is what people share, and it is the cheapest to
verify. Rust (Bevy-ready logic) ships for 2048 as proof that the protocol is engine-neutral. Godot and Unity ports are
welcome but count as verified only when a headless runner passes the cases.

**Three small open-source games first.** 2048 (MIT), the Chrome Dino (BSD-3-Clause) and Canvas Bird (MIT) have source we
may run and redistribute, are small enough to verify completely, and cover pure logic, physics with timing, and
black-box observation of a game whose state is private.

**No art, sound or names from an original.** Rebuilds draw their own shapes. See `NOTICE`.

**The repository was built unattended.** The first version was written in one session while the author was away;
everything that could be checked was checked (see `docs/STATUS.md`), and what was not is listed there.

```

rea-games itself is MIT licensed (see LICENSE).

The folder originals/ holds unmodified copies of the open-source games that the recordings are made from.
They stay under their own licences, and each folder keeps its licence file:

  originals/2048          2048, (c) 2014 Gabriele Cirulli, MIT        https://github.com/gabrielecirulli/2048
  originals/dino          t-rex-runner (a copy of Chromium's offline
                          dinosaur game), BSD-3-Clause                https://github.com/wayou/t-rex-runner
  originals/canvas-bird   Canvas Bird, (c) 2016 Yiotis Kaltsikis, MIT https://github.com/giotiskl/Canvas-Bird
  originals/blocks        javascript-tetris, (c) 2011-2016 Jake Gordon
                          and contributors, MIT                       https://github.com/jakesgordon/javascript-tetris

The rebuilds in games/*/ports are written from the behavior specs in games/*/GAME.md. They use none of the originals'
code, art or sound. The names 2048 and "Dino" describe the games being studied; this project is not affiliated with
their authors or with Google. The falling-blocks game is called "blocks" here: Tetris is a registered
trademark of its owner, this project is not affiliated with it, and the rebuild uses no Tetris name or art.

The recordings (games/*/cases) are measurements of how the originals behave: input lists, random numbers and
resulting game states.

Part of a family: [rea](https://github.com/morluto/rea) takes software apart, [rea-video](https://github.com/JuneYaooo/rea-video)
does it for video, [craft-anything](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything) rebuilds apps, and
[rust-anything](https://github.com/erkamyaman/rust-anything) proves a Rust rewrite behaves like the original.
**rea-games does it for games.**

## Play the rebuilds

In your browser, no install: **[erkamyaman.github.io/rea-games](https://erkamyaman.github.io/rea-games/)**

Each is written from a behavior spec (`GAME.md`), draws its own art, and passes its recording.

| Game | Original | Play | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2048 | [gabrielecirulli/2048](https://github.com/gabrielecirulli/2048), MIT | [play it](https://erkamyaman.github.io/rea-games/play/2048.html) | 19 cases, 24,044 inputs: web, Godot and Rust (Bevy) ports |
| Dino | Chrome's offline dinosaur ([copy](https://github.com/wayou/t-rex-runner), BSD-3) | [play it](https://erkamyaman.github.io/rea-games/play/dino.html) | 29 cases, 63,000 frames: web, Godot and Rust (Bevy) ports |
| Canvas Bird | [giotiskl/Canvas-Bird](https://github.com/giotiskl/Canvas-Bird), MIT | [play it](https://erkamyaman.github.io/rea-games/play/canvas-bird.html) | 30 cases, 68,409 frames: web, Godot and Rust (Bevy) ports |
| Blocks (falling blocks) | [jakesgordon/javascript-tetris](https://github.com/jakesgordon/javascript-tetris), MIT | `docs/play/blocks.html` | 36 cases, 104,208 frames: web, Godot and Rust (Bevy) ports |

## How it works

```
original game ──(fake clock, seeded random numbers)──> cases/*.json   inputs + every random number + state after each step
                                                                          │
GAME.md  (what the recording shows)  ──> your port, in any engine  ──> rea-games verify  ──> identical, or the first difference
```

1. **Record.** The original runs unmodified. Its clock and `Math.random` are replaced from outside, so a run can be repeated. Every random number it draws is saved (the *tape*), with the inputs and the game state after each step.
2. **Spec.** `GAME.md` states the rules, the order of operations in a frame, the constants, the quirks (including the original's bugs) and what is not modelled.
3. **Port.** Any program that reads a case on stdin and prints `{trace, tapeUsed}` is a port: JavaScript, Rust, Godot run headless, C#.
4. **Verify.** Every recorded state must match exactly, and the port must use exactly the recorded random numbers. The first difference is printed with its path.

```
$ node bin/rea-games.mjs verify all
2048 / web          => 19/19 cases identical, 24044 inputs
2048 / bevy         => 19/19 cases identical, 24044 inputs
2048 / godot        => 19/19 cases identical, 24044 inputs
canvas-bird / web   => 30/30 cases identical, 68409 inputs
canvas-bird / godot => 30/30 cases identical, 68409 inputs
canvas-bird / bevy  => 30/30 cases identical, 68409 inputs
dino / web          => 29/29 cases identical, 63000 inputs
dino / godot        => 29/29 cases identical, 63000 inputs
dino / bevy         => 29/29 cases identical, 63000 inputs
blocks / web        => 36/36 cases identical, 104208 inputs
blocks / godot      => 36/36 cases identical, 104208 inputs
blocks / bevy       => 36/36 cases identical, 104208 inputs
```

A check that cannot fail proves nothing, so each port was also broken on purpose (a constant, a collision offset, a timing gate, a spawn-gap factor): `verify` failed each time, for example 5 of 30 Canvas Bird cases pass with the 30 fps gate changed, 3 of 19 for 2048 with the spawn odds changed from 0.9 to 0.8.

## Use it with an agent

```
claude plugin marketplace add erkamyaman/rea-games
claude plugin install rea-games@rea-games
```

Then: *"rea this game: <link to an open-source game>, rebuild it in Godot."* The skill (`skills/rea-games/SKILL.md`) runs the loop above. It records, writes the spec, builds the port, verifies, and reports what it could not cover.

Or by hand:

```
node bin/rea-games.mjs list
node bin/rea-games.mjs new my-game        # scaffold games/my-game
node bin/rea-games.mjs record my-game     # run the original, write the cases
node bin/rea-games.mjs verify my-game --port web
node bin/rea-games.mjs pack all           # gzip the cases for git
```

Needs Node 22. Browser games also need Playwright with Chromium; the Rust ports need `cargo`, the Godot one a Godot 4.4 binary (`REA_GODOT=/path/to/godot`).

## Engines

| Target | Status |
|---|---|
| Web (canvas, one HTML file, mobile friendly) | all three games, verified |
| Rust / Bevy | 2048, Dino, Canvas Bird and Blocks as Bevy projects (`dino-core` logic verified through `dino-runner`; the Bevy window itself compiles and ran 25 s under Xvfb, never played) |
| Godot 4.4 (GDScript) | 2048, Dino, Canvas Bird and Blocks, verified: a headless runner passes all 19 cases. A playable scene (`ports/godot/main.tscn`) loads and takes input in a headless smoke test; its look has not been checked |
| Unity (C#) | not started |
| Capacitor (wrap the web build for iOS/Android) | not started; Capacitor wraps a web build, so it builds on the web ports |

A port counts as verified only when `verify` runs it through its runner. Ports that are not verified are labelled as such.

## Legal, in short

Rebuilding behavior from a recording is clean-room work. Originals are included only where their licence allows it, unmodified, with their licence (`NOTICE`). Rebuilds use no art, sound, names or code from the originals. If you add a game, check its licence first and do not use a trademarked name.

## What it does not do (yet)

- It matches **behavior**, not looks: the rebuilds draw their own art.
- Games must be runnable and deterministic once their clock and random numbers are controlled. Network games, and games whose state cannot be observed from outside, need more work.
- Coverage is what the cases hit. Each `GAME.md` lists the gaps (for Dino: few crashes into the flying obstacle; for Canvas Bird: few hits on the bottom pipe).

Details: [`docs/STATUS.md`](docs/STATUS.md) · [`DECISIONS.md`](DECISIONS.md) · [`docs/pitfalls.md`](docs/pitfalls.md) · [`NOTICE`](NOTICE)

`bin/rea-games.mjs`:

```mjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
// rea-games: record a game's original, check a port against the recording.
import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
import { listGames, loadGame, verifyPort, packCases } from "../lib/verify.mjs";
import { scaffold } from "../lib/scaffold.mjs";

const root = path.join(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const [cmd, ...rest] = process.argv.slice(2);
const flag = (n) => { const i = rest.indexOf(n); return i < 0 ? null : rest.splice(i, 2)[1] ?? true; };

const help = `rea-games: reverse-engineer a game's behavior, then check a rebuild against it

  rea-games list                        games, their ports and recorded cases
  rea-games new <game>                  scaffold games/<game> (game.json, record.mjs, GAME.md, port stub)
  rea-games record <game>               run the original and write cases/*.json
  rea-games pack <game|all>             gzip the cases (the repository keeps them packed)
  rea-games verify <game|all> [--port web|rust|...]   replay every case through a port
`;

async function main() {
  if (!cmd || cmd === "help" || cmd === "--help") return console.log(help);
  if (cmd === "list") {
    for (const g of listGames(root)) {
      const { meta } = loadGame(root, g);
      console.log(`${g.padEnd(12)} original: ${meta.original.repo} (${meta.original.license})  ports: ${Object.keys(meta.ports).join(", ")}`);
    }
    return;
  }
  if (cmd === "new") {
    console.log("created", scaffold(root, rest[0] ?? ""));
    return;
  }
  if (cmd === "record") {
    const g = rest[0];
    const { dir, meta } = loadGame(root, g);
    const cd = path.join(dir, "cases");
    if (fs.existsSync(cd)) for (const f of fs.readdirSync(cd)) if (f.endsWith(".json.gz")) fs.rmSync(path.join(cd, f)); // packed copies would go stale
    const mod = await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(dir, meta.record)).href);
    console.log(`recorded ${g}:`, await mod.record());
    return;
  }
  if (cmd === "pack") {
    for (const g of rest[0] === "all" || !rest[0] ? listGames(root) : [rest[0]]) {
      const r = packCases(root, g);
      console.log(`${g}: ${(r.before / 1e6).toFixed(1)} MB -> ${(r.after / 1e6).toFixed(1)} MB`);
    }
    return;
  }
  if (cmd === "verify") {
    const portOpt = flag("--port");
    const names = rest[0] === "all" || !rest[0] ? listGames(root) : [rest[0]];
    let bad = 0;
    for (const g of names) {
      const { meta } = loadGame(root, g);
      for (const p of portOpt && portOpt !== true ? [portOpt] : Object.keys(meta.ports)) {
        console.log(`${g} / ${p}`);
        const r = verifyPort(root, g, p);
        console.log(`  => ${r.passed}/${r.cases} cases identical, ${r.inputs} inputs, ${r.frames} recorded states`);
        bad += r.failures.length;
      }
    }
    process.exit(bad ? 1 : 0);
  }
  console.error(help);
  process.exit(2);
}
main().catch((e) => { console.error(e.message); process.exit(1); });

```

`docs/STATUS.md`:

```md
# Status

What works today and how it was checked. Numbers are what `node bin/rea-games.mjs verify all` printed on the day this
was written (Linux container, Node 22, Chromium from Playwright). Nothing here was run on macOS or Windows.

## Verified

| Game | Port | Cases | Inputs / frames | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2048 | web (JS) | 19 | 24,044 inputs | all identical |
| 2048 | Rust (`game2048-core` through `game2048-runner`) | 19 | 24,044 inputs | all identical |
| 2048 | Godot 4.4.1 (GDScript, headless) | 19 | 24,044 inputs | all identical |
| Dino | web (JS) | 29 | 63,000 frames | all identical, exact comparison |
| Dino | Godot 4.4.1 (GDScript, headless) | 29 | 63,000 frames | all identical, exact comparison |
| Dino | Rust (`dino-core` through `dino-runner`) | 29 | 63,000 frames | all identical, exact comparison |
| Canvas Bird | web (JS) | 30 | 68,409 frames | all identical, exact comparison |
| Canvas Bird | Godot 4.4.1 (GDScript, headless) | 30 | 68,409 frames | all identical, exact comparison |
| Canvas Bird | Rust (`bird-core` through `bird-runner`) | 30 | 68,409 frames | all identical, exact comparison |

Comparison is exact (no rounding, no tolerance) and also requires the port to use exactly the recorded random numbers.

**The check was shown to fail** when a port is broken: 2048 (spawn odds 0.9 to 0.8: 3 of 19 pass; win threshold changed:
3 cases fail), Canvas Bird (jump speed, collision window, 30 fps gate: 6, 16, 5 of 30 pass), Dino (gravity, head-box
width, gap factor, flying-obstacle speed, an extra acceleration on the crash frame: 28, 3, 28, 7 and 21 cases fail).

**Dino cosmetic randomness cannot change the trace**: `node games/dino/record.mjs --visual` replays every case with two
other seeds for clouds, stars and blinking; traces and tapes were identical.

## Playable pages

`docs/play/*.html` are single files made by `node scripts/bundle.mjs`. 2048 was opened from `file://` in headless
Chromium without console errors and played a few moves. Dino and Canvas Bird pages were loaded at desktop and phone width
by their authors with no errors; they have not been played by a person.

## 2048 Bevy port

`game2048-core` through `game2048-runner` is verified (spawn odds 0.9 to 0.8: 3 of 19 pass; win threshold 2048 to 4096: 16 of 19 pass). The Bevy window (0.19, 2D) compiles, and a screenshot taken under Xvfb with software rendering shows the board and tile numbers. Keys, swipe, restart and keep-playing were not tried; only the starting board was seen. The tile colours are the web port's own dark palette, not the original's. This port replaced the earlier plain-Rust 2048 runner, which had the same logic and no window.

## Dino engine ports: what is and is not proven

- Godot: logic and runner verified. Godot's JSON parser is off by one digit on some decimals, so the runner reads the case text itself. Breaking gravity failed every case. Replacing the JS-style `round` with Godot's own still passed 29/29: the recordings never hit a negative `.5` tie, so that rounding is correct by construction but not covered. The scene was run headless only; nobody looked at it.
- Rust/Bevy: `dino-core` through `dino-runner` verified (gravity, pterodactyl speed and rounding breaks all failed). The Bevy front end (`dino-bevy`, Bevy 0.19.1, 2D only, score in the window title) compiles and ran 25 s under Xvfb with software rendering without a panic; frames were not looked at and keys, jump, duck and restart were not tried. Bevy 0.20.1 needs a newer rustc than the build machine had. Building `dino-runner` does not compile Bevy; running or checking `dino-bevy` needs system packages (Wayland, udev, xkbcommon, Vulkan drivers on Linux).

## Canvas Bird engine ports: what is and is not proven

- Godot: verified. Breaking force, jump speed and the hit-box offset made 2, 6 and 16 of 30 cases pass. Narrowing the hit window by one pixel still passed: pipes always sit at x = 1 mod 3, so that boundary is never reached by any recording (an equivalent mutant, not a check failure). The runner rebuilds JavaScript's shortest-digit number text; one tiny exponent-form value in the recording relies on Godot's own `to_float`, and it matches. The scene was smoke-tested headless only.
- Rust/Bevy: `bird-core` through `bird-runner` verified (force, fall limit and gap breaks all failed; the same hit-window mutant survives for the same reason). The Bevy window (0.19.1) compiles and ran 20 s under Xvfb without a crash; nobody looked at it or played it. Score is shown in the window title.

## Blocks (falling blocks)

| Game | Port | Cases | Frames | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Blocks | web (JS) | 36 | 104,208 | all identical, exact comparison |
| Blocks | Godot 4.4.1 (GDScript, headless) | 36 | 104,208 | all identical, exact comparison |
| Blocks | Rust (`blocks-core` through `blocks-runner`) | 36 | 104,208 | all identical, exact comparison |

Recorded from the unmodified original (MIT) with a fake clock and its random piece bag taped: 142 games, 109 losses, 3,271 locked pieces, line clears of 1, 2, 3 and 4 rows (461, 79, 23, 20), all 28 piece/rotation pairs, 993 blocked rotations. Breaking a piece shape, the speed formula, a rotation rule or the 4-line score made `verify` fail each time on every port (for example 26, 17, 11 and 6 of 36 cases failed on the web port). The demo GIF shows 152 of 152 frames identical, and a separate run matched all 3,500 steps of a case.

Gaps: the original's "second drop in the frame that loses" appears in only 3 recorded frames, and a full top row is never reached. The original has no pause. The Godot scene was smoke-tested headless only; the Bevy window compiled and one software-rendered screenshot shows the court, a piece, the next-piece preview and the score text, but no keys were sent. The game is called "blocks" because Tetris is a registered trademark; see `NOTICE`.

## Gaps (read before quoting any number)

- **Coverage is what the cases hit.** Dino: only 7 crashes into the flying obstacle, none while speed-dropping; no
  touch/mouse input, blur/focus, other canvas widths, or a restart in the frame right after a crash. Canvas Bird: 11 hits on
  the bottom pipe, no hit where the pipe in range is not the "next" one, at most one click per frame, dt between 8 and
  100 ms. 2048: sizes other than 4x4 and animations are not modelled.
- Dino cap-speed runs are rare (3 of 29 cases) because they need about 3,500 frames without a crash.
- The Dino and Canvas Bird originals are small copies of open-source projects (see `NOTICE`), not the commercial games.
- Dino's first key press starts a second update chain in the original (two updates per frame); the port reproduces it.
  It was found by comparing, and is written up in `games/dino/GAME.md`.
- Unity and Bevy ports do not exist yet. The Godot port covers 2048 only. Its playable scene (`main.tscn`) was loaded
  headless and fed key presses without errors; nobody has looked at it on screen. Godot 4.4.1 was downloaded from the
  official release and checked against the published SHA-512 before use. Breaking the GDScript port (spawn odds, win
  threshold) made 16 and 3 of 19 cases pass, so the check bites there too.
- The repository has not been pushed anywhere. Cases are stored gzipped (`rea-games pack`).
- The agent plugin manifest (`.claude-plugin`) was written from the documented format and has not been installed in
  Claude Code. The Codex plugin format is not provided; `AGENTS.md` points Codex at the skill.
- `node games/dino/record.mjs --visual` reads unpacked `cases/*.json`; run `rea-games record dino` first (it also clears packed copies).
- CI (`.github/workflows/verify.yml`) has never run.

```

`docs/pitfalls.md`:

```md
# Pitfalls

Mistakes already made in this repository, each with the rule that prevents it. Add one in the same change whenever a
mistake is worth not repeating.

**A fixture with wrong tile positions made the original misbehave.** 2048 moves tiles by their own `x`/`y`, not by their
place in the grid, so a saved game built with every `position.x = 0` produced a trace no sane port could match. Build
fixtures so every field agrees with the cell it sits in, and look at a few steps of each hand-made case.

**A stale snapshot was recorded as truth.** 2048's `keepPlaying` never calls the actuator, so the last actuated state
still said "terminated" and the port correctly said it was not. Read state from the live game object, not from the
last callback.

**Comparing JSON as text failed a correct Rust port.** `serde_json` sorts keys, JavaScript keeps insertion order, and every
case "differed". Compare parsed values (`lib/compare.mjs`), never `JSON.stringify` output.

**CI never reached `verify all`.** The Godot checksum line turned `<hash>  Godot_v...zip` into `<hash>   godot.zip`
(three spaces), so `sha512sum -c` looked for a file named ` godot.zip` and every run failed before any port was replayed.
Replace only the file name in the sums line, and look at a new workflow's log for the `verify` output, not just its
colour.

**A check that cannot fail looks like a pass.** After a port is green, break it three ways (a constant, a branch, an
offset) and watch `verify` fail each time; otherwise the cases may not reach the code you think they do.

```

(() => {
const __mod0 = (() => {
// 2048, written from games/2048/GAME.md. Cells are stored as cells[x][y] (column first),
// the same layout the recording uses, so snapshots compare directly.
const SIZE = 4;
const DIRS = [[0, -1], [1, 0], [0, 1], [-1, 0]]; // up, right, down, left as (dx, dy)

class Game2048 {
  constructor({ rng = Math.random, initial = null } = {}) {
    this.rng = rng;
    this.best = 0;
    this.load(initial);
  }

  load(saved) {
    if (saved) {
      this.cells = saved.grid.cells.map((col) => col.map((t) => (t ? t.value : 0)));
      ({ score: this.score, over: this.over, won: this.won, keepPlaying: this.kept } = saved);
    } else {
      this.cells = Array.from({ length: SIZE }, () => Array(SIZE).fill(0));
      this.score = 0;
      this.over = this.won = this.kept = false;
      this.addTile();
      this.addTile();
    }
    this.best = Math.max(this.best, this.score);
  }

  get terminated() { return this.over || (this.won && !this.kept); }

  restart() { this.load(null); }
  keepPlaying() { this.kept = true; }

  empty() {
    const out = [];
    for (let x = 0; x < SIZE; x++) for (let y = 0; y < SIZE; y++) if (!this.cells[x][y]) out.push([x, y]);
    return out;
  }

  addTile() {
    const free = this.empty();
    if (!free.length) return;
    const value = this.rng() < 0.9 ? 2 : 4; // the value is drawn before the place
    const [x, y] = free[Math.floor(this.rng() * free.length)];
    this.cells[x][y] = value;
  }

  // Slide one line toward its start. A tile merges at most once per move, and the pair
  // nearest the wall merges first.
  slide(line) {
    const tiles = line.filter(Boolean);
    const out = [];
    let gained = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < tiles.length; i++) {
      if (tiles[i] === tiles[i + 1]) {
        out.push(tiles[i] * 2);
        gained += tiles[i] * 2;
        if (tiles[i] * 2 === 2048) this.won = true;
        i++;
      } else out.push(tiles[i]);
    }
    while (out.length < SIZE) out.push(0);
    return { out, gained };
  }

  move(dir) {
    if (this.terminated) return false;
    const [dx, dy] = DIRS[dir];
    let moved = false;
    for (let k = 0; k < SIZE; k++) {
      // the k-th line, listed from the wall the tiles move toward
      const coords = [];
      for (let i = 0; i < SIZE; i++) {
        const j = dx + dy > 0 ? SIZE - 1 - i : i; // moving right or down: the wall is at the end
        coords.push(dx !== 0 ? [j, k] : [k, j]);
      }
      const { out, gained } = this.slide(coords.map(([x, y]) => this.cells[x][y]));
      coords.forEach(([x, y], i) => {
        if (this.cells[x][y] !== out[i]) moved = true;
        this.cells[x][y] = out[i];
      });
      this.score += gained;
    }
    if (!moved) return false;
    this.addTile();
    if (!this.hasMoves()) this.over = true;
    this.best = Math.max(this.best, this.score);
    return true;
  }

  hasMoves() {
    if (this.empty().length) return true;
    for (let x = 0; x < SIZE; x++) for (let y = 0; y < SIZE; y++) {
      const v = this.cells[x][y];
      if ((x + 1 < SIZE && this.cells[x + 1][y] === v) || (y + 1 < SIZE && this.cells[x][y + 1] === v)) return true;
    }
    return false;
  }

  snapshot() {
    return {
      grid: this.cells.map((c) => c.slice()),
      score: this.score, over: this.over, won: this.won, terminated: this.terminated, best: this.best,
    };
  }
}

return { SIZE, Game2048 };
})();

const { Game2048, SIZE } = __mod0;

const board = document.getElementById("board");
const cells = [];
for (let y = 0; y < SIZE; y++) for (let x = 0; x < SIZE; x++) { const c = document.createElement("div"); c.className = "cell"; board.append(c); cells.push([x, y, c]); }
function draw() {
  const s = game.snapshot();
  for (const [x, y, c] of cells) { const v = s.grid[x][y]; c.textContent = v || ""; c.className = "cell" + (v ? " " + (v <= 2048 ? "v" + v : "vbig") : ""); }
  score.textContent = s.score; best.textContent = s.best;
  const msg = document.getElementById("msg");
  msg.classList.toggle("on", s.terminated);
  msgtitle.textContent = s.over ? "Game over" : "You made 2048";
  keep.style.display = s.over ? "none" : "";
}
const key = { ArrowUp:0, w:0, ArrowRight:1, d:1, ArrowDown:2, s:2, ArrowLeft:3, a:3 };
addEventListener("keydown", (e) => { if (e.key in key) { e.preventDefault(); game.move(key[e.key]); draw(); } });
let t0 = null;
addEventListener("touchstart", (e) => { t0 = e.touches[0]; }, { passive: true });
addEventListener("touchend", (e) => {
  if (!t0) return; const t = e.changedTouches[0]; const dx = t.clientX - t0.clientX, dy = t.clientY - t0.clientY; t0 = null;
  if (Math.max(Math.abs(dx), Math.abs(dy)) < 24) return;
  game.move(Math.abs(dx) > Math.abs(dy) ? (dx > 0 ? 1 : 3) : (dy > 0 ? 2 : 0)); draw();
});
restart.onclick = again.onclick = () => { game.restart(); draw(); };
keep.onclick = () => { game.keepPlaying(); draw(); };
window.__game = game; window.__draw = draw;

<script>
(() => {
// Blocks: the rules of the falling-blocks puzzle, as pure logic. No DOM, no clock, no Math.random:
// the caller hands in `rng` (a function returning [0,1)) and calls step({dt, keys}) once per frame.
// Written from games/blocks/GAME.md (what the original does, observed and read), not copied.

const W = 10, H = 20;
const KINDS = "ijlostz";
// four rotations of a 4x4 mask each, bit 0x8000 is the top-left cell, rows run left to right
const SHAPES = {
  i: { size: 4, masks: [0x0f00, 0x2222, 0x00f0, 0x4444] },
  j: { size: 3, masks: [0x44c0, 0x8e00, 0x6440, 0x0e20] },
  l: { size: 3, masks: [0x4460, 0x0e80, 0xc440, 0x2e00] },
  o: { size: 2, masks: [0xcc00, 0xcc00, 0xcc00, 0xcc00] },
  s: { size: 3, masks: [0x06c0, 0x8c40, 0x6c00, 0x4620] },
  t: { size: 3, masks: [0x0e40, 0x4c40, 0x4e00, 0x4640] },
  z: { size: 3, masks: [0x0c60, 0x4c80, 0xc600, 0x2640] },
};
const START_STEP = 0.6, STEP_DECREMENT = 0.005, MIN_STEP = 0.1; // seconds per row of gravity
const T0 = 1000000; // the recording's clock starts here (ms)

// the cells (column, row) a piece covers
function cellsOf(kind, x, y, dir) {
  const out = [];
  const mask = SHAPES[kind].masks[dir];
  for (let i = 0; i < 16; i++) if (mask & (0x8000 >> i)) out.push([x + (i & 3), y + (i >> 2)]);
  return out;
}

class Blocks {
  constructor({ rng, clock0 = T0 }) {
    this.rng = rng;
    this.t = clock0;              // the page's clock, ms; frames add dt to it and read the whole milliseconds
    this.last = Math.floor(clock0);
    this.bag = [];                // piece letters still in the bag, in splice order
    this.cur = null;
    this.nxt = null;
    this.reset();                 // the page resets once while it loads
  }

  // ---- pieces
  newPiece() {
    if (this.bag.length === 0) for (const k of KINDS) for (let n = 0; n < 4; n++) this.bag.push(k);
    // the original asks for a float in [0, len-1) and splice truncates it: the bag's last piece is never
    // the one taken until it is the only one left
    const kind = this.bag.splice(Math.floor(this.rng() * (this.bag.length - 1)), 1)[0];
    const x = Math.round(this.rng() * (W - SHAPES[kind].size));
    return { type: kind, x, y: 0, dir: 0 };
  }

  blocked(kind, x, y, dir) {
    for (const [cx, cy] of cellsOf(kind, x, y, dir)) {
      if (cx < 0 || cx >= W || cy < 0 || cy >= H || this.grid[cy][cx]) return true;
    }
    return false;
  }

  // ---- game state changes
  reset() {
    this.dtAcc = 0;
    this.actions = [];
    this.grid = Array.from({ length: H }, () => Array(W).fill(null));
    this.setRows(0);
    this.score = 0;
    this.vscore = 0;
    this.cur = this.nxt || this.newPiece();
    this.nxt = this.newPiece();
  }
  setRows(n) {
    this.rows = n;
    this.stepSec = Math.max(MIN_STEP, START_STEP - STEP_DECREMENT * n);
  }
  play() { this.reset(); this.playing = true; }
  lose() { this.vscore = this.score; this.playing = false; }

  move(dx, dy) {
    const c = this.cur;
    if (this.blocked(c.type, c.x + dx, c.y + dy, c.dir)) return false;
    c.x += dx; c.y += dy;
    return true;
  }
  rotate() {
    const c = this.cur;
    const d = (c.dir + 1) & 3;
    if (!this.blocked(c.type, c.x, c.y, d)) c.dir = d; // no kicks: a blocked turn is dropped
  }

  // gravity step and the soft-drop key: one row down, or lock the piece
  drop() {
    if (this.move(0, 1)) return;
    const c = this.cur;
    this.score += 10;
    for (const [cx, cy] of cellsOf(c.type, c.x, c.y, c.dir)) this.grid[cy][cx] = c.type;
    this.removeLines();
    this.cur = this.nxt;
    this.nxt = this.newPiece();
    this.actions = [];
    if (this.blocked(this.cur.type, this.cur.x, this.cur.y, this.cur.dir)) this.lose();
  }

  removeLines() {
    let n = 0;
    // rows 19..1 are checked; row 0 is never looked at (a full top row would stay)
    for (let y = H - 1; y > 0; y--) {
      if (this.grid[y].every((c) => c)) {
        for (let r = y; r > 0; r--) this.grid[r] = this.grid[r - 1].slice();
        this.grid[0] = Array(W).fill(null);
        y++; // look at the same row again
        n++;
      }
    }
    if (n > 0) {
      this.setRows(this.rows + n);
      this.score += 100 * 2 ** (n - 1);
    }
  }

  // ---- one rendered frame
  key(name) {
    if (this.playing) {
      if (name === "left") this.actions.push("left");
      else if (name === "right") this.actions.push("right");
      else if (name === "up") this.actions.push("up");
      else if (name === "down") this.actions.push("down");
      else if (name === "esc") this.lose();
      // "play" is the start link; it works in any state (the page hides it while playing)
      else if (name === "play") this.play();
    } else if (name === "space" || name === "play") this.play();
  }

  step({ dt, keys = [] }) {
    for (const k of keys) this.key(k);
    this.t += dt;
    const now = Math.floor(this.t);
    const idt = Math.min(1, (now - this.last) / 1000);
    this.last = now;
    if (!this.playing) return;
    if (this.vscore < this.score) this.vscore += 1;
    const a = this.actions.shift();
    if (a === "left") this.move(-1, 0);
    else if (a === "right") this.move(1, 0);
    else if (a === "up") this.rotate();
    else if (a === "down") this.drop();
    this.dtAcc += idt;
    // the piece may have been replaced (or the game lost) by the action above; gravity still runs
    if (this.dtAcc > this.stepSec) {
      this.dtAcc -= this.stepSec;
      this.drop();
    }
  }

  snapshot() {
    const DIRS = { up: 0, right: 1, down: 2, left: 3 };
    const p = (c) => ({ type: c.type, x: c.x, y: c.y, dir: c.dir });
    return {
      grid: this.grid.map((r) => r.map((c) => c || ".").join("")),
      current: p(this.cur),
      next: p(this.nxt),
      bag: this.bag.join(""),
      score: this.score, vscore: this.vscore, rows: this.rows, step: this.stepSec, dt: this.dtAcc,
      playing: !!this.playing,
      actions: this.actions.map((a) => DIRS[a]),
    };
  }
}



(function main() {
  const STEP = 1000 / 60;      // the rules are stepped at 60 Hz whatever the screen does
  const COLORS = { i: "#4fd1e8", j: "#5b7cfa", l: "#ff9f43", o: "#f7d046", s: "#5fd068", t: "#b565e8", z: "#f0544f" };
  const cv = document.getElementById("c"), ctx = cv.getContext("2d");
  const nv = document.getElementById("nextc"), nctx = nv.getContext("2d");
  const CELL = cv.width / W; // 30
  const $ = (id) => document.getElementById(id);

  // ---- game (a recorded tape replaces Math.random when a driver sets window.__tape)
  const TAPE = Array.isArray(window.__tape) ? window.__tape : null;
  let used = 0;
  const rng = TAPE ? () => { if (used >= TAPE.length) throw new Error("tape used up"); return TAPE[used++]; } : Math.random;
  const game = new Blocks({ rng, clock0: TAPE ? 1000000 : Math.floor(performance.now()) });
  let best = 0;
  try { best = +localStorage.getItem("blocks-best") || 0; } catch {}
  let keys = [];
  let started = false, over = false;

  function press(k) { keys.push(k); }
  function tick(dt = STEP) {
    const wasPlaying = game.playing;
    game.step({ dt, keys });
    keys = [];
    if (wasPlaying && !game.playing) { over = true; remember(); }
    if (game.playing) { started = true; over = false; }
  }
  function remember() {
    if (game.score > best) { best = game.score; try { localStorage.setItem("blocks-best", String(best)); } catch {} }
  }

  // ---- drawing: flat squares with a light top edge, no textures
  function square(c, x, y, size, color, alpha = 1) {
    c.globalAlpha = alpha;
    c.fillStyle = color; c.beginPath(); c.roundRect(x + 1, y + 1, size - 2, size - 2, 5); c.fill();
    c.fillStyle = "rgba(255,255,255,.22)"; c.fillRect(x + 4, y + 3, size - 8, 3);
    c.globalAlpha = 1;
  }
  function draw() {
    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, cv.width, cv.height);
    ctx.strokeStyle = "rgba(255,255,255,.05)"; ctx.lineWidth = 1;
    for (let x = 1; x < W; x++) { ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x * CELL + .5, 0); ctx.lineTo(x * CELL + .5, cv.height); ctx.stroke(); }
    for (let y = 1; y < H; y++) { ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(0, y * CELL + .5); ctx.lineTo(cv.width, y * CELL + .5); ctx.stroke(); }
    for (let y = 0; y < H; y++) for (let x = 0; x < W; x++) { const k = game.grid[y][x]; if (k) square(ctx, x * CELL, y * CELL, CELL, COLORS[k]); }
    const c = game.cur;
    if (game.playing) {
      let gy = c.y; while (!game.blocked(c.type, c.x, gy + 1, c.dir)) gy++; // where it would land
      if (gy !== c.y) for (const [x, y] of cellsOf(c.type, c.x, gy, c.dir)) square(ctx, x * CELL, y * CELL, CELL, COLORS[c.type], .22);
      for (const [x, y] of cellsOf(c.type, c.x, c.y, c.dir)) square(ctx, x * CELL, y * CELL, CELL, COLORS[c.type]);
    }
    // next piece, centred in a 5x5 preview
    nctx.clearRect(0, 0, nv.width, nv.height);
    const n = game.nxt, u = nv.width / 5, pad = (5 - 4) / 2;
    const cs = cellsOf(n.type, 0, 0, 0);
    const minx = Math.min(...cs.map((q) => q[0])), maxx = Math.max(...cs.map((q) => q[0])), miny = Math.min(...cs.map((q) => q[1])), maxy = Math.max(...cs.map((q) => q[1]));
    const ox = (5 - (maxx - minx + 1)) / 2 - minx, oy = (5 - (maxy - miny + 1)) / 2 - miny;
    for (const [x, y] of cs) square(nctx, (x + ox) * u, (y + oy) * u, u, COLORS[n.type]);
    void pad;
    $("score").textContent = String(Math.floor(game.vscore));
    $("rows").textContent = String(game.rows);
    $("best").textContent = String(Math.max(best, game.score));
    const msg = $("msg");
    msg.classList.toggle("off", !!game.playing);
    if (!game.playing) {
      $("msgtitle").textContent = over ? "Game over" : "Blocks";
      $("msgsub").textContent = (over ? game.score + " points, " + game.rows + " rows. " : "") + "Press Space or tap to play";
    }
  }

  // ---- input
  const MAP = { ArrowLeft: "left", ArrowRight: "right", ArrowUp: "up", ArrowDown: "down", Escape: "esc", " ": "space" };
  document.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
    const k = MAP[e.key];
    if (!k) return;
    e.preventDefault();
    press(k);
  });
  $("msg").addEventListener("pointerdown", (e) => { e.preventDefault(); press("space"); });
  $("restart").addEventListener("click", () => { press("play"); $("restart").blur(); });
  for (const b of document.querySelectorAll("#pad button")) {
    let timer = null;
    const stop = () => { clearInterval(timer); timer = null; };
    b.addEventListener("pointerdown", (e) => {
      e.preventDefault();
      press(b.dataset.k);
      if (b.dataset.k !== "up") timer = setInterval(() => press(b.dataset.k), 90); // hold to repeat
    });
    for (const ev of ["pointerup", "pointercancel", "pointerleave"]) b.addEventListener(ev, stop);
  }

  // ---- frame loop
  let last = null, acc = 0;
  function frame(ts) {
    if (last === null) last = ts;
    acc += Math.min(ts - last, 250);
    last = ts;
    if (!TAPE) while (acc >= STEP) { tick(); acc -= STEP; }
    draw();
    requestAnimationFrame(frame);
  }
  if (TAPE) window.__rea = {
    // one frame of a recorded case: step(dt, keys)
    step(dt, k = []) { keys = k.slice(); tick(dt); draw(); return game.snapshot(); },
    snapshot: () => game.snapshot(),
    tapeUsed: () => used,
  };
  document.addEventListener("visibilitychange", () => { last = null; });
  requestAnimationFrame(frame);
})();

})();
</script>
</body>
</html>

<script>
(() => {
const __mod0 = (() => {
// Canvas Bird, rebuilt from games/canvas-bird/GAME.md. Pure logic: no DOM, no clock, no Math.random.
// createBird({ rng }) takes a random source and returns a game that advances one rendered frame per
// step({ dt, click }) and returns that frame's draw list (the strings described in driver.mjs).
// The clock is a number the game advances itself by dt, so a replay is exact.
const T0 = 1000000;

const W = 640, H = 480;
const PIPES = 5, SPACING = 300, GAP = 120, MIN_OFF = -150, MAX_OFF = 50, PIPE_SPEED = 3;
const PIPE_W = 64, PIPE_H = 316;
const BIRD = { x: 70, w: 64, h: 64, startY: 20, startV: 2, force: 0.15, jump: -6, maxV: 8 };
const FRAME_MS = 1000 / 30;

function createBird({ rng, start = T0 }) {
  let t = start;
  const now = () => Math.floor(t);
  const randInt = (lo, hi) => Math.floor(rng() * (hi - lo + 1) + lo);

  let playing = false; // a round is on screen (splash text is hidden)
  let controls = false; // taps flap and pipes score; false once the bird has hit something
  let score = 0;
  let alpha = 1, rising = false;
  let strokeStyle = "#000000", fillStyle = "#000000";
  const bg = [{ x: 0 }, { x: W }];
  const bird = { y: BIRD.startY, v: BIRD.startV, sprite: 0 };
  let spriteClock = now(); // when the sprite frame last changed
  const fallClock = now(); // set once and never moved: this is why the 30 fps gate stops mattering
  let pipes = [];
  let next = 0, last = PIPES - 1;
  let out = [];

  const addPipe = (i, off) => ({
    id: i,
    up: { x: W + i * SPACING, y: H / 2 + GAP + off },
    down: { x: W + i * SPACING, y: 0 - GAP + off },
    off,
  });
  function setupPipes() {
    next = 0; last = PIPES - 1; pipes = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < PIPES; i++) pipes.push(addPipe(i, randInt(MIN_OFF, MAX_OFF)));
  }

  function scoreCheck(p, x) {
    if (p.id === next && x + PIPE_W < BIRD.x + BIRD.w) {
      next = next === PIPES - 1 ? 0 : next + 1;
      if (controls) { score++; out.push("a:point"); }
    }
  }
  function moveUp(p) {
    p.up.x -= PIPE_SPEED;
    if (p.up.x <= -PIPE_W) {
      p.up.x = p.down.x = pipes[last].up.x + SPACING;
      p.off = randInt(MIN_OFF, MAX_OFF); // drawn y is NOT recomputed from it (see GAME.md)
      last = last === PIPES - 1 ? 0 : last + 1;
    }
    scoreCheck(p, p.up.x);
  }
  function moveDown(p) {
    p.down.x -= PIPE_SPEED;
    scoreCheck(p, p.down.x);
  }

  function collided() {
    const right = BIRD.x + BIRD.w, top = bird.y, bottom = bird.y + BIRD.h;
    const p = pipes[next];
    const px = p.down.x + 40, gapTop = p.down.y + PIPE_H, gapBottom = p.up.y;
    let hit = false;
    if (right > px && right < px + PIPE_W - 40) {
      if (top < gapTop || bottom > gapBottom) hit = true;
    }
    if (bottom < 0 || top > H) hit = true;
    if (hit && controls) out.push("a:lose");
    return hit;
  }

  function spriteFrame() {
    const n = now();
    if (n - spriteClock > FRAME_MS) {
      spriteClock = n;
      bird.sprite++;
      if (bird.sprite > 2) bird.sprite = 0;
    }
    return bird.sprite;
  }

  function draw() {
    out = [];
    out.push(`c:0:0:${W}:${H}`);
    for (const b of bg) out.push(`i:background:${b.x}:0`);
    for (const b of bg) { b.x -= 1; if (b.x <= -W) b.x = W; }
    if (!playing) {
      strokeStyle = `rgba(0,0,0,${alpha})`;
      out.push(`t:stroke:Click to start game:${W / 2 - 230}:80:${strokeStyle}`);
      fillStyle = `rgba(255,255,255,${alpha})`;
      out.push(`t:fill:Click to start game:${W / 2 - 230}:80:${fillStyle}`);
      if (alpha < 0) rising = true;
      if (alpha > 1) rising = false;
      alpha += rising ? 0.02 : -0.02;
    } else {
      for (const p of pipes) {
        out.push(`i:enemy_up:${p.up.x}:${p.up.y}`);
        out.push(`i:enemy_down:${p.down.x}:${p.down.y}`);
        moveUp(p);
        moveDown(p);
      }
      const sx = spriteFrame() * BIRD.w;
      out.push(`s:player:${sx}:0:${BIRD.w}:${BIRD.h}:${BIRD.x}:${bird.y}:${BIRD.w}:${BIRD.h}`);
      if (now() - fallClock > FRAME_MS) {
        if (bird.v < BIRD.maxV) bird.v += BIRD.force;
        bird.y += bird.v;
      }
      if (collided()) {
        controls = false;
        if (bird.y - BIRD.h > H) playing = false;
      }
      fillStyle = "black";
      out.push(`t:stroke:${score}:${W / 2 - 11}:51:${strokeStyle}`);
      fillStyle = "white";
      out.push(`t:fill:${score}:${W / 2 - 10}:50:${fillStyle}`);
    }
    return out;
  }

  function click() {
    if (controls) bird.v = BIRD.jump;
    if (!playing) {
      score = 0; bird.v = BIRD.startV; bird.y = BIRD.startY;
      setupPipes();
      playing = true;
      controls = true;
    }
  }

  return {
    // the frame the page draws when it loads, before any step
    load: () => draw(),
    step({ dt, click: clicked = false }) {
      if (clicked) click();
      t += dt;
      return draw();
    },
    // what a renderer with its own art needs
    view: () => ({ playing, controls, score, alpha, bird: { x: BIRD.x, y: bird.y, v: bird.v, sprite: bird.sprite }, pipes, next, bg }),
  };
}

return { T0, createBird };
})();

const { createBird } = __mod0;
const W = 640, H = 480;
const cv = document.getElementById("c");
const ctx = cv.getContext("2d");

// that recorded tape and window.__rea.step(dt) advances one recorded frame (the page's own loop then idles).

// ---- sound: tiny beeps, only after the first tap (browsers need a gesture)
let ac = null;
function beep(freq, len, type = "square", gain = 0.05) {
  try {
    ac = ac || new (window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext)();
    const o = ac.createOscillator(), g = ac.createGain();
    o.type = type; o.frequency.value = freq; g.gain.value = gain;
    o.connect(g); g.connect(ac.destination);
    g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, ac.currentTime + len);
    o.start(); o.stop(ac.currentTime + len);
  } catch {}
}

cv.addEventListener("pointerdown", tap);
addEventListener("keydown", (e) => { if (e.code === "Space" || e.code === "ArrowUp" || e.code === "Enter") { if (!e.repeat) tap(e); } });

sky.addColorStop(0, "#4fb3ff"); sky.addColorStop(0.7, "#bfe7ff"); sky.addColorStop(1, "#ffe9b8");

function cloud(x, y, s) {
  for (const [dx, dy, rx, ry] of [[0, 0, 36, 16], [26, -10, 26, 18], [-24, -6, 22, 14]]) {
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.ellipse(x + dx * s, y + dy * s, rx * s, ry * s, 0, 0, 7); ctx.fill();
  }
}
function drawBackground(v) {
  ctx.fillStyle = sky; ctx.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);
  const off = v.bg[0].x; // scrolls 1 px a frame, like the original
  ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(255,255,255,.85)";
  for (const k of [0, 1]) for (const [x, y, s] of clouds) cloud(((x + off * (0.4 + 0.5 * s) + k * W + W * 2) % (W * 1.2)) - 60, y, s);
  ctx.fillStyle = "#7ccf79";
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(0, H);
  for (let x = 0; x <= W; x += 20) ctx.lineTo(x, H - 26 - 10 * Math.sin((x - off * 2) / 55));
  ctx.lineTo(W, H); ctx.fill();
  ctx.fillStyle = "#5bb461"; ctx.fillRect(0, H - 14, W, 14);
}
function pipeBody(x, y, h, capAtBottom) {
  const g = ctx.createLinearGradient(x, 0, x + 64, 0);
  g.addColorStop(0, "#2f9e44"); g.addColorStop(0.35, "#69db7c"); g.addColorStop(1, "#2b8a3e");
  ctx.fillStyle = g;
  ctx.fillRect(x + 5, y, 54, h);
  const cy = capAtBottom ? y + h - 26 : y;
  ctx.fillRect(x, cy, 64, 26);
  ctx.strokeStyle = "#1b5e2b"; ctx.lineWidth = 2;
  ctx.strokeRect(x + 5, y, 54, h); ctx.strokeRect(x, cy, 64, 26);
}
function drawPipes(v) {
  for (const p of v.pipes) { pipeBody(p.down.x, p.down.y, 316, true); pipeBody(p.up.x, p.up.y, 316, false); }
}
function drawBird(v) {
  const b = v.bird;
  ctx.save();
  ctx.translate(b.x + 32, b.y + 32);
  ctx.rotate(Math.max(-0.5, Math.min(1.1, b.v / 9)));
  ctx.fillStyle = "#ffd43b"; ctx.strokeStyle = "#e67700"; ctx.lineWidth = 3;
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.ellipse(0, 0, 28, 24, 0, 0, 7); ctx.fill(); ctx.stroke();
  const wing = [-6, 0, 8][b.sprite];
  ctx.fillStyle = "#fcc419";
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.ellipse(-8, 4 + wing * 0.5, 14, 8, -0.3 + wing * 0.04, 0, 7); ctx.fill(); ctx.stroke();
  ctx.fillStyle = "#fff"; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(14, -8, 8, 0, 7); ctx.fill();
  ctx.fillStyle = "#212529"; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(16, -8, 3.5, 0, 7); ctx.fill();
  ctx.fillStyle = "#ff6b35"; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(22, -1); ctx.lineTo(38, 4); ctx.lineTo(22, 10); ctx.closePath(); ctx.fill();
  ctx.restore();
}
function label(text, x, y, size, alpha = 1) {
  ctx.font = `800 ${size}px system-ui, sans-serif`;
  ctx.textAlign = "center";
  ctx.lineWidth = size / 6; ctx.lineJoin = "round";
  ctx.strokeStyle = `rgba(20,30,50,${alpha})`; ctx.strokeText(text, x, y);
  ctx.fillStyle = `rgba(255,255,255,${alpha})`; ctx.fillText(text, x, y);
}
function render() {
  const v = game.view();
  ctx.setTransform(cv.width / W, 0, 0, cv.height / H, 0, 0);
  drawBackground(v);
  if (!v.playing) {
    if (over) { label("Game over", W / 2, 150, 54); label(`Score ${lastScore}   Best ${best}`, W / 2, 205, 26); }
    label("Tap to " + (over ? "play again" : "start"), W / 2, over ? 290 : 120, 38, Math.max(0.25, Math.min(1, v.alpha)));
    drawBird({ bird: { x: 70, y: 200 + Math.sin(performance.now() / 280) * 8, v: 0, sprite: (performance.now() / 120 | 0) % 3 } });
  } else {
    drawPipes(v); drawBird(v);
    label(String(v.score), W / 2, 62, 52);
  }
}

// ---- loop: the original's physics is per rendered frame (tuned at 60 fps), so run it on a fixed 60 Hz step
const STEP = 1000 / 60;
let acc = 0, prev = performance.now();
function advance(dt) {
  const out = game.step({ dt, click: clickPending });
  if (clickPending && ac === null) beep(1, 0.01, "sine", 0.0001);
  if (clickPending) beep(520, 0.06);
  clickPending = false;
  if (out.includes("a:point")) beep(880, 0.12, "triangle", 0.08);
  if (out.includes("a:lose")) beep(160, 0.35, "sawtooth", 0.08);
  const v = game.view();
  if (v.playing) { lastScore = v.score; wasPlaying = true; }
  else if (wasPlaying) {
    wasPlaying = false; over = true;
    if (lastScore > best) { best = lastScore; bestEl.textContent = best; try { localStorage.setItem("canvas-bird-best", best); } catch {} }
  }
  return out;
}
function frame(now) {
  acc += Math.min(100, now - prev); prev = now;
  if (!TAPE) while (acc >= STEP) { acc -= STEP; advance(STEP); }
  render();
  requestAnimationFrame(frame);
}
if (TAPE) game.load(); // the original draws one frame when it loads, before any step
if (TAPE) window.__rea = { step(dt) { const out = advance(dt); render(); return out; }, tapeUsed: () => tapeUsed };
requestAnimationFrame(frame);

})();

<script>
(() => {
const __mod0 = (() => {
// Chrome Dino gameplay, rebuilt from games/dino/GAME.md. Pure logic: no DOM, no clock, no Math.random.
//   rng()  returns the next gameplay random number in [0, 1) (the recorded tape, or Math.random)
//   step({dt, jump, duck, jumpUp, duckUp, enter, animEnd})  one browser frame:
//          the clock moves by dt ms, the key events of the frame run, then the pending
